title: Edit file content-version conflicts and interrupted-write recovery

categories.prompt: Two edits use the same original inode and content version while a mutation hook allows one edit to finish first.

executableTestNames: preserves independent edits from two same-inode writers
returns an actionable conflict when an external edit removes the requested text
does not broaden replace_all when the same-inode match count changes

categories.prompt: Replace the path, symlink, parent directory, or access grant during an edit, and interrupt an in-place write before retrying.

executableTestNames: rejects a regular inode replacement while the edit is awaiting its baseline hook
rejects a symlink swap before writing through the original descriptor
preserves recovery evidence without touching the replacement when a symlink swaps at commit
rejects a parent-directory rebind even when the replacement entry is a hard link to the same inode
honors access-profile revocation while the edit is awaiting its baseline hook
updates hard links in place and preserves inode and mode
retains before and after bytes without overwriting a partial descriptor write failure
does not write during recovery when the parent binding changes
preserves a process-killed write until explicit reconciliation then permits the next edit
preserves external post-kill bytes %j and retains the recovery record
rejects a forged private receipt without changing the target
does not recover a partial target while its receipt owner process is still live
preserves ambiguous recovery bytes %j instead of restoring a snapshot
preserves an external writer's ambiguous bytes %j during failure handling
blocks another process editing a hardlink alias of an active transaction
reconciles exact completed bytes through a hardlink without restoring older content
applies the file size guardrail to each version when enabled=%s
rejects the independent recovery cap before allocating or mutating a disabled-guardrail file

notes: Executable Vitest coverage uses temporary real files, descriptors, hard links, separate processes, SIGKILL, and a private user-data directory with no Electron app. Recovery never restores ambiguous bytes automatically; exact known states reconcile without rewriting the file. Cross-process coordination is confined to one active user-data profile. The JSON links to runtime tests; it is not itself graded by run_eval_suite.cjs.
